title: ITDR release notes, 2023 to 2026, as dated entries

prose.text: This subject records what the dated entries of the Zscaler ITDR Release Upgrade Summary pages say, and not what the product does now {{gap:current-behaviour}}. [[identity-protection.overview]] is the hub for the current behaviour.

checks.do: Which dated entry a release-note statement comes from before presenting it, since each claim here says what that entry says.

2026-01-09-guardduty-role.statement: In the release note dated January 09, 2026: the command to create a role for Amazon GuardDuty containment was updated to create a common role to access the AWS account instead of a tenant-specific role.

quotes: January 09, 2026
The command to create a role for Amazon GuardDuty containment is updated to create a common role to access the AWS account instead of a tenant-specific role.

2025-11-04-attribute-collection.statement: In the release note dated November 04, 2025: Attribute Collection was enabled by default for all Active Directory scan configurations, including for customers who had it disabled.

quotes: November 04, 2025
Attribute Collection is enabled for all Active Directory scan configurations by default. This change applies to all customers, including customers who have been disabled in their environment.

2025-11-04-ui-changes.statement: In the release note dated November 04, 2025: an icon to access error logs was added for server agents and endpoint agents, and the Tenant Name field in the Tenant Details window was renamed Tenant ID.

quotes: November 04, 2025
An icon to access error logs was added for server agents and endpoint agents.
In the Tenant Details window, the Tenant Name field was renamed to Tenant ID.

2025-08-18-privileged-account-tracking.statement: In the release note dated August 18, 2025: Active Directory Privileged Account Tracking was added; it monitors anomalous login activity using a machine learning system, accepts up to 200 user accounts per AD domain for explicit tracking in addition to default privileged users, and lets incidents be marked safe to prevent future alerts for similar behavior.

quotes: August 18, 2025
monitors anomalous login activity of users using a machine learning system
In addition to default privileged users, you can add up to 200 user accounts per AD domain for explicit tracking.
you can mark the incidents as safe to prevent future alerts for similar behavior

2025-08-18-pdf-reports.statement: In the release note dated August 18, 2025: the Entra ID Executive Summary, AD Executive Summary, Entra ID Delta, Active Directory Delta and Endpoint Credential Exposure PDF reports were enhanced, and the two Executive Summary reports gained change detection information.

quotes: August 18, 2025
The following PDF reports are enhanced to improve clarity in analyzing the report data:
Additionally, the Entra ID and Active Directory (AD) Executive Summary reports include change detection information to help you track modifications within Entra ID and AD domains.
- Entra ID Executive Summary Report
- AD Executive Summary Report
- Entra ID Delta Report
- Active Directory Delta Report
- Endpoint Credential Exposure Report

2025-08-18-server-threat-detection.statement: In the release note dated August 18, 2025: server agent-based threat detection gained four detections: Account Reconnaissance, Password Spray, External IP Authentication (DC) and Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly, the last described as checking anomalous Kerberos service ticket requests using machine learning.

quotes: August 18, 2025
Account Reconnaissance: An attack technique used by adversaries to use known username dictionaries to exploit authentication errors and discover valid usernames.
Password Spray: An attack technique used by adversaries to attempt to gain access to multiple user accounts with commonly used passwords.
External IP Authentication (DC): An attack technique used by adversaries to identify login attempts from public IP addresses
Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly: Checks anomalous Kerberos service ticket requests using machine learning.

2025-08-18-tab-renames.statement: In the release note dated August 18, 2025: Settings > User & Roles > SSO was renamed IdP Providers, Settings > Users & Roles > Support Users was renamed Zscaler Remote Assistance, and Settings > Advanced Settings > Maintenance was renamed Manage Events & Evidence.

quotes: August 18, 2025
| Settings > User & Roles > SSO | Settings > User & Roles > IdP Providers |
| Settings > Users & Roles > Support Users | Settings > Users & Roles > Zscaler Remote Assistance |
| Settings > Advanced Settings > Maintenance | Settings > Advanced Settings > Manage Events & Evidence |

2025-06-23-ad-remediations.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: Active Directory Remediations were added, requiring a configured server agent and allowing actions on specific or multiple identities in bulk; the actions were Enable User, Disable User, Reset Password and Revoke Group Membership, with remediation logs available afterwards.

quotes: You must configure a server agent to run AD remediation actions. You can run remediation actions for specific or multiple identities (in bulk).
- Enable User
- Disable User
- Reset Password
- Revoke Group Membership
After remediation, you can view remediation logs
evidence.after: The Active Directory (AD) Remediations feature allows you to run remediation actions

2025-06-23-identity-search.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: Identity Search was added to search identities across Active Directory, Entra ID and Okta on a single page, by username, first name, last name, email address and more, with results correlated with ITDR posture information.

quotes: The Identity Search feature allows you to search for specific identities across identity platforms—including Active Directory (AD), Entra ID, and Okta—all on a single page.
You can search for identities by username, first name, last name, email address, and more.
These identities are correlated and enriched with information from Zscaler ITDR posture capabilities

2025-06-23-servicenow.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: ITDR integration with ServiceNow was added, allowing an incident to be created on the AD Posture, AD Change Detection, Endpoint Credential Exposure, Entra ID Posture and Entra ID Change Detection dashboards.

quotes: You can create a ServiceNow incident for an issue and track it in the ServiceNow portal.
- Active Directory Posture dashboard
- Entra ID Change Detection dashboard
- Active Directory Change Detection dashboard
- Endpoint Credential Exposure dashboard
- Entra ID Posture dashboard

2025-06-23-okta-log-retention.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: Okta system logs for threat detection were stated to be retained for only 14 days, with the retention period not modifiable.

quotes: Okta system logs for threat detection are only retained for 14 days. You cannot modify this retention period.

2025-06-23-server-threat-detection.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: threat detection on a domain controller through a server agent was added, covering DCSync, DCShadow, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, Suspicious DPAPI access, Suspicious Group Additions and Brute Force.

quotes: The threat detection feature enables you to detect threats on a domain controller using a server agent.
- DCSync: An attack that allows an adversary
- DCShadow: An attack in which an adversary registers a fake AD domain controller
- Kerberoasting: A pervasive attack technique targeting AD service account credentials.
- AS-REP roasting: An attack in which an adversary targets accounts that have disabled Kerberos pre-authentication.
- Suspicious DPAPI access: Suspicious attempts to retrieve domain backup keys from a domain controller.
- Suspicious Group Additions: Attempts to establish persistence by adding malicious users to privileged groups in an organization's domain.
- Brute Force: An attack method used to gain unauthorized access to AD accounts.

2025-06-23-dashboard-renames.statement: In the release note dated June 23, 2025: the dashboards Identity Posture, Change Detection, Entra ID and Identity Risk Summary were renamed Active Directory Posture, Active Directory Change Detection, Entra ID Posture and Risk Summary.

quotes: | Identity Posture | Active Directory Posture |
| Change Detection | Active Directory Change Detection |
| Entra ID | Entra ID Posture |
| Identity Risk Summary | Risk Summary |

2025-04-14-mark-unsafe.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: an event or attacker could be marked as unsafe, which removes the allowlist rules and flags the attacker for further investigation.

quotes: April 14, 2025
When you mark an event or attacker as unsafe, the allowlist rules are removed, and the attacker is flagged for further investigation.

2025-04-14-dns-hostname-criteria.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: DNS Hostname (Specific) and DNS Hostname (RegEx) were added as endpoint selection criteria for endpoint credential exposure and threat detection policies, selecting by complete FQDN or by a regular expression for the FQDN.

quotes: April 14, 2025
| DNS Hostname (Specific) | Select endpoints based on their FQDNs by specifying the complete FQDN value |
| DNS Hostname (RegEx) | Select endpoints based on their FQDNs by specifying a regular expression for the FQDN value |

2025-04-14-lsa-protections.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: the Local Security Authority (LSA) Protections scan type was added, which checks registry keys to confirm whether LSA protection is enabled and can be enabled or disabled when configuring the endpoint credential exposure scan.

quotes: April 14, 2025
The Local Security Authority (LSA) Protections scan type was added to check the registry keys to confirm if LSA protection is enabled.
You can enable or disable the LSA Protections scan type when configuring the endpoint credential exposure scan.

2025-04-14-password-reuse.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: Password Reuse Analysis was added, showing on the Password Analysis dashboard the percentage of AD users who have reused passwords in pie charts for regular and privileged users, with a Summary tab count of other AD user accounts that share the same password excluding the affected user.

quotes: April 14, 2025
On the Password Analysis dashboard (ITDR > Dashboard > Password Analysis), you can view the percentage of Active Directory (AD) users who have reused passwords.

On the Summary tab (ITDR > Identity Posture > Top 10 Users & Computers > User), you can view the total number of other AD user accounts that share the same password as the affected AD user. This count excludes the affected AD user.
The data is represented in pie charts for both regular and privileged users.

2025-04-14-entra-role-types.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: posture checks for Entra ID identities supported both active and eligible role assignment types, with the role assignment type shown on the Roles > Entra tab of an affected identity.

quotes: April 14, 2025
Posture checks for Entra ID identities support both active and eligible role assignment types, providing an effective approach to role monitoring.
For an affected Entra ID identity, you can view the role assignment type on the Roles > Entra tab.

2025-04-14-allowlisted-rules.statement: In the release note dated April 14, 2025: when an event or attacker is marked as safe due to an allowlist rule, the specific rule that triggered the action can be viewed on the Event Logs page.

quotes: April 14, 2025
When an event or attacker is marked as safe due to an allowlist rule, you can view the specific rule that triggered the action on the Event Logs page.

2025-03-05-delta-reports.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: AD and Entra ID Scan Delta Reports were added, comparing two historical scans to show newly introduced risks, resolved issues and updates to existing risks, downloadable in PDF or Excel formats.

quotes: March 05, 2025
You can automatically compare two historical scans and download the delta report to identify newly introduced risks, resolved issues, and updates to the existing risks.
You can download these delta reports in PDF or Excel formats for offline review

2025-03-05-copy-columns.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: copying specific table columns, up to 1,000 rows, to paste into CSV, JSON, Notepad or other compatible files was added across modules.

quotes: March 05, 2025
You can copy specific columns from tables (up to 1,000 rows) and paste them into CSV, JSON, Notepad, or other compatible files across various modules

2025-03-05-credex-types.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: the Windows OOBE Priv Esc, Windows OOBE Files and Unmanaged Local Admins scan or exposure types were added; Browser cookies, Saved Browser Credentials, LSASS Application secrets, LSASS Login Sessions, Insecure UAC Settings, Active Sessions, Recent Run Commands, Recent Powershell Commands and Certificate Files were removed; and Cached Domain Logon Credentials gained credential cleanup support.

quotes: March 05, 2025
- Windows OOBE Priv Esc
- Windows OOBE Files
- Unmanaged Local Admins
- Browser cookies - Removed
- Saved Browser Credentials
- LSASS Application secrets
- LSASS Login Sessions
- Insecure UAC Settings
- Active Sessions
- Recent Run Commands
- Recent Powershell Commands
- Certificate Files
The Cached Domain Logon Credentials scan or exposure type supports the credential cleanup feature.

2025-03-05-credex-dashboard.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: the Endpoint Credential Exposure dashboard gained a domain risk category or severity level, the top 5 credential exposure issues, severity and risk charts and a Risk Reduction Roadmap; a Detailed Findings page was added; and the Severity column was removed from the Identities page table.

quotes: March 05, 2025
Details of the top 5 credential exposure issues that exist on your endpoints.
Risk Reduction Roadmap.
The Detailed Findings page (ITDR > Dashboard > Endpoint Credential Exposure > Detailed Findings) was added.
The Severity column was removed from the table on the Identities page
Domain risk category or severity level (Critical, High, Medium, Low, etc.).
Credential exposure issues categorized by severity in a bar chart.
Credential exposure issues categorized by risk in a donut chart.
evidence.after: The following sections were added to the Endpoint Credential Exposure dashboard

2025-03-05-entra-remediations.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: Entra ID Remediations were added with the actions Disable User, Revoke Session, Enforce MFA, Enforce MFA or phishing-resistant MFA, Remove Active Role Assignment and Remove Group Membership, and permissions for running them can be added or removed while deploying the script in the Azure portal.

quotes: March 05, 2025
- Disable User
- Revoke Session
- Enforce MFA
- Enforce MFA or phishing-resistant MFA
- Remove Active Role Assignment
- Remove Group Membership
You can add or remove permissions for running remediation actions while deploying a script in the Azure portal.
evidence.after: The Entra ID Remediation Action feature allows you to automatically run remediation actions

2025-03-05-export-event-fields.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: ITDR supported exporting all event fields in JSON format.

quotes: March 05, 2025
ITDR supports exporting event fields in JSON format.
You can export all the event fields and use them for further analysis and investigation.

2025-03-05-guardduty-integration.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: integration with Amazon GuardDuty was added to isolate and contain attackers who interact with decoys by blocking access to those users across AWS resources.

quotes: March 05, 2025
Zscaler ITDR supports integration with Amazon GuardDuty to isolate and contain attackers who interact with decoys by blocking access to those users across AWS resources.

2025-03-05-risk-reduction-roadmap.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: the Risk Reduction Roadmap was added for AD, Entra ID and endpoints, letting you assess the current domain risk severity (Critical, High, Medium or Low) and set a target severity level for a prioritized remediation roadmap.

quotes: March 05, 2025
assess the current domain risk severity (Critical, High, Medium, or Low), and set a target severity level to systematically lower the domain risk
After the target severity level is set, ITDR provides an actionable and prioritized risk and remediation roadmap.
The Risk Reduction Roadmap feature provides a proactive security approach to enhance the security posture of your identity infrastructure, including Active Directory (AD), Entra ID, and endpoints.

2025-03-05-zpa-containment-zidentity.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: ZPA containment support was extended to Authentication Service-enabled tenants, where a contained user cannot reach real apps and only app decoys remain accessible.

quotes: March 05, 2025
Support for containment with Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) is extended to Authentication Service-enabled tenants.
If a user is contained with ZPA, then real apps become inaccessible and only app decoys remain accessible.

2025-03-05-server-agent-la.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: Active Directory Monitoring with Server Agent was listed under Feature in Limited Availability.

quotes: March 05, 2025
Feature in Limited Availability
Active Directory Monitoring with Server Agent

2025-03-05-server-agent-session-password.statement: In the release note dated March 05, 2025: the server agent entry said session tracking can be enabled in the server agent policy to monitor logon activities for all AD administrators and privileged accounts, and that password analysis can be enabled and configured in the policy, with the analysis done locally on the selected domain controller and not leaving the customer environment.

quotes: March 05, 2025
You can enable session tracking in the server agent policy to monitor logon activities for all AD administrators and privileged accounts.
You can enable and configure password analysis in the server agent policy to identify compromised or weak passwords
The analysis is done locally on the selected domain controller (DC) and does not leave the customer environment

2024-12-04-attribute-collection.statement: In the release note dated December 04, 2024: ITDR attribute collection was described: AD user and computer attributes such as objectSid, description, pwdLastSet and department are collected by the Windows endpoint agent assigned to scan the domain once collection is enabled, while Entra ID attribute collection is enabled by default after a tenant is connected.

quotes: December 04, 2024
ITDR collects AD object (user and computer) attributes, such as objectSid, description, pwdLastSet, department, etc.
The Windows endpoint agent assigned for scanning the AD domain collects the attributes.
After you connect an Entra ID tenant with ITDR for scanning, the attribute collection is enabled by default.
After you configure an AD domain for scanning, you can enable attribute collection.

2024-12-04-remediation-flowchart.statement: In the release note dated December 04, 2024: when an issue has multiple remediations, a remediation flowchart was added that prioritizes the most suitable remediation first; it can be exported as an SVG file and AD objects can be added to the safelist.

quotes: December 04, 2024
The workflows in the flowchart are prioritized based on the most suitable remediation to the issue. The most appropriate remediation is listed first, followed by the less suitable ones.
You can export the remediation chart as an SVG file and add AD objects to the safelist.
If there are multiple remediations for an issue, Zscaler ITDR provides a flowchart that breaks down multiple steps into distinct workflows.

2024-10-15-entra-posture-checks.statement: In the release note dated October 15, 2024: new Entra ID posture checks were added for best practice violations for applications, multi-factor authentication, insecure privilege management and data loss.

quotes: October 15, 2024
The posture checks are related to best practice violations for applications, multi-factor authentication (MFA), insecure privilege management, data loss, etc.

2024-08-14-credex-cleanup-types.statement: In the release note dated August 14, 2024: credential cleanup of exposed endpoint credentials was added for these exposure or scan types only: Saved Windows Credentials, AWS Credentials, Azure Credentials, Google Cloud Credentials, Database Connections, Saved VNC Passwords and Admin AutoLogon Settings.

quotes: August 14, 2024
Currently, ITDR supports credential cleanup for the following exposure or scan types only:
- Saved Windows Credentials
- AWS Credentials
- Azure Credentials
- Google Cloud Credentials
- Database Connections
- Saved VNC Passwords
- Admin AutoLogon Settings

2024-08-14-safelist-expiration.statement: In the release note dated August 14, 2024: an expiration date could be set when adding an item to a safelist, after which the item is added back into scan results, and objects in the safelist are not counted towards risk scoring.

quotes: August 14, 2024
This ensures that safelisted objects are automatically added back for consideration in scan results after the expiration date.
Objects in the safelist are not counted towards risk scoring.
You can configure an expiration date while adding an item to the safelist.

2024-08-14-custom-change-detection.statement: In the release note dated August 14, 2024: custom change detection policies were added for critical property changes in AD (users, groups, computers) and Entra ID (users, service principals, roles) identities, with specific users notified when changes pertaining to a policy are detected.

quotes: August 14, 2024
You can configure change detection policies to detect when changes to critical properties in Active Directory (AD) and Entra ID identities are made.
You can create policies based on various properties across users, groups, and computers to detect AD changes.
You can create policies based on various properties across users, service principals, and roles to detect Entra ID changes.
In addition, you can notify specific users when the changes pertaining to a policy are detected.

2024-08-14-ui-renames.statement: In the release note dated August 14, 2024: Focus Area was renamed Detailed Findings and Recommendations, Add to Safelist was renamed Add Issue to Safelist, the Active Directory Vulnerability report was renamed Active Directory Posture Scan Report, and the LDAP Activity module in AD Threat Detection Policies was renamed Suspicious LDAP Activity.

quotes: August 14, 2024
Focus Area was renamed to Detailed Findings and Recommendations on the Active Directory
Add to Safelist was renamed to Add Issue to Safelist on the Detailed Findings and Recommendations
The Active Directory Vulnerability report (ITDR > Identity Posture > View Report) was renamed to Active Directory Posture Scan Report.
The LDAP Activity module in Active Directory Threat Detection Policies was renamed to Suspicious LDAP Activity.

2024-07-08-notifications.statement: In the release note dated July 08, 2024: ITDR Notifications were added to email executive summary reports or bad change details to configured recipients after AD domains, Entra ID tenants and endpoints are scanned.

quotes: the configured recipients receive emails with executive summary reports or bad changes details.
After AD domains, Entra ID tenants, and endpoints are scanned for vulnerabilities

2024-07-08-safelist-relocation.statement: In the release note dated July 08, 2024: all safelists moved from the Settings module to ITDR > Settings, with Active Directory Posture Safelist renamed Active Directory Issue Safelist, Change Detection Safelist renamed AD Change Detection Issue Safelist and Entra ID Posture Safelist renamed Entra ID Issue Safelist.

quotes: All safelists were moved from the Settings module to ITDR > Settings along with some UI label changes:
Active Directory Posture Safelist was renamed to Active Directory Issue Safelist.
Change Detection Safelist was renamed to AD Change Detection Issue Safelist.
Entra ID Posture Safelist was renamed to Entra ID Issue Safelist.

2024-06-05-entra-id-posture.statement: In the release note dated June 05, 2024: ITDR - Microsoft Entra ID was added, with an Entra ID tenant connected and scanned from ITDR > Manage > Entra ID, a dashboard at ITDR > Dashboard > Entra ID, and change classification as good, bad or info.

quotes: You can connect an Entra ID tenant and run a scan from the Entra ID configuration page (ITDR > Manage > Entra ID).
The impact of the changes are classified as good, bad, or info.
the results are displayed on a dashboard for further investigation and remediation.
the results are available on the Entra ID dashboard (ITDR > Dashboard > Entra ID).

2024-06-05-credex-scan-type-toggle.statement: In the release note dated June 05, 2024: after configuring an endpoint credential exposure scan, scan types that run on the endpoints could be enabled or disabled.

quotes: After you configure an endpoint credential exposure scan, you can enable or disable scan types that run on the endpoints to identify exposed credentials.

2024-06-05-identity-risk-summary.statement: In the release note dated June 05, 2024: the Identity Risk Summary dashboard was added, collating top or critical misconfigurations and vulnerabilities from identity solutions such as Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID together with top endpoint credential exposures, with MITRE ATT&CK mappings.

quotes: The Identity Risk Summary dashboard collates top or critical misconfigurations and vulnerabilities from various identity management solutions, such as Active Directory (AD), Microsoft Entra ID, etc.
It also identifies the top endpoint credential exposures contributing to identity risk posture.
You can also view mappings to security risk frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK.

2024-04-17-okta-ai-containment.statement: In the release note dated April 17, 2024: containment integration with Identity Threat Protection with Okta AI was added, pushing user risk scores to Okta using the Shared Signals Framework (SSF) so that Okta, based on the score and Okta policies, can end sessions, prompt an MFA challenge or invoke a workflow.

quotes: April 17, 2024
You can integrate Zscaler ITDR with Okta to push user risk scores by leveraging the Shared Signals Framework (SSF).

Based on the risk score and Okta policies, Okta can end the user’s sessions, prompt a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) challenge, or invoke a workflow to restore your organization's security posture.

2024-04-17-credex-scan-data.statement: In the release note dated April 17, 2024: endpoint credential exposure scan data could be downloaded as a .zip file containing a CSV file for each credential exposure issue.

quotes: April 17, 2024
a .zip file containing CSV files for each credential exposure issue

2024-04-17-phone-sms-removed.statement: In the release note dated April 17, 2024: ITDR no longer supported phone and text message notifications, and the Phone and SMS options were removed from rules, the notification template options were removed, and the phone field was removed from User Details and Edit Profile.

quotes: April 17, 2024
Zscaler ITDR no longer supports phone and text message notifications.
Under Orchestrate > Rules, the Phone and SMS notification options were removed from the Rule Details window.
Under Settings > Users, the phone field was removed from the User Details window.
Under Orchestrate > Event Templates, the phone and text message notification template options were removed.
Under Account Settings > Profile, the phone field was removed from the Edit Profile section.

2024-04-17-okta-threat-detection.statement: In the release note dated April 17, 2024: Okta identity system logs identified as potentially suspicious could be viewed under the Okta tab on the Threats page.

quotes: April 17, 2024
You can view the Okta identity system logs across Okta that are identified as potentially suspicious under the Okta tab on the Threats page.

2024-02-14-safe-process-regex.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: safe processes could be added using regular expressions, so a single safe process can match multiple processes by a pattern in the process names.

quotes: February 14, 2024
This allows you to configure a single safe process that accommodates multiple different processes by matching a specific pattern of strings in the process names.

2024-02-14-show-all-agents.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: a Show all agents toggle was added under the Actions menu on the Endpoint Settings Agents page to list active and inactive endpoint agents.

quotes: February 14, 2024

On the Agents page (Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents), a Show all agents toggle was added under the Actions drop-down menu. This allows you to view a list of active and inactive endpoint agents in the Agents table.

2024-02-14-investigate-actions.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: the Investigate module was described with per-event actions Contain with Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Contain with Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), Mark as safe, Add to blocklist and Delete an event, and extended details of ThreatParse, Chronology and Event Logs.

quotes: February 14, 2024
- Contain with Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)
- Contain with Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)
- Mark as safe
- Add to blocklist
- Delete an event
- Event Logs: Provides log information for all events associated with the selected component.
ThreatParse: Provides information on all attacks based on MITRE framework reconstructed in natural English.
Chronology: Provides a temporal overview of events and a heatmap of the activities.

2024-02-14-orchestrate.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: Orchestrate was described as creating and managing rules, API tokens and event notification templates, and integrating with security solutions to transmit event logs in real time, contain threats and enrich security events.

quotes: February 14, 2024
Create and manage rules that automate workflows, notifications, and containment in response to threat detection.
Create and manage API tokens and event notification templates.
Transmit event logs in real time.
Contain threats to isolate active attackers.
Enrich security events with relevant contextual information to manage security threats efficiently.

2024-02-14-ui-moves.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: Deceive > Landmine Agents > Agents, Settings, Update Phase Groups and Safe Processes moved to Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents, Agent Configuration, Agent Update Groups and Safe Processes, and ITDR > Scan Agents moved to ITDR > Manage > Active Directory Posture.

quotes: February 14, 2024
| Deceive > Landmine Agents > Agents | Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents |
| Deceive > Landmine Agents > Settings | Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agent Configuration |
| Deceive > Landmine Agents > Update Phase Groups | Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agent Update Groups |
| Deceive > Landmine Agents > Safe Processes | Settings > Endpoint Settings > Safe Processes |
| ITDR > Scan Agents | ITDR > Manage > Active Directory Posture |

2024-02-14-okta-zia-zpa-integrations.statement: In the release note dated February 14, 2024: ITDR integrations were described: Okta for viewing identity metadata, identifying real-time changes and acting on an Okta identity, and ZIA and ZPA for traffic violation insights on the AD user account and for containment.

quotes: February 14, 2024
You can integrate ITDR with Okta to view Okta identity metadata, identify real-time changes, and perform actions on an Okta identity in the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
You can integrate ITDR with ZIA and ZPA to gain insights into traffic violations or bad activities on ZIA or ZPA services for the Active Directory user account.
You can also contain an attack or threat and forward the attack details to ZIA or ZPA to take further actions according to the defined policy.

2023-11-02-assessment-report.statement: In the release note dated November 02, 2023: the ITDR Active Directory Assessment Posture report was added, showing a unified domain risk score on a scale of 0 to 100, the most prevalent risk types and an issue priority matrix, and downloadable as a PDF file.

quotes: November 02, 2023
The report displays a unified domain risk score on a scale of 0 to 100, the type of risks most prevalent in the AD, an issue priority matrix, and remediation guidance to fix the issues.
You can download the ITDR AD Assessment Posture report as a PDF file.

2023-11-02-change-detection-safelist.statement: In the release note dated November 02, 2023: a Change Detection Safelist was added so detected change detection issues can be reviewed and marked as safe.

quotes: November 02, 2023
You can review these change detection issues to confirm that they are not a risk and mark them as safe.

2023-11-02-ui-renames.statement: In the release note dated November 02, 2023: the Identity label on the left-side navigation was renamed to ITDR.

quotes: November 02, 2023
The Identity label on the left-side navigation menu was renamed to ITDR.

2023-08-31-ad-attack-detection.statement: In the release note dated August 31, 2023: a Windows landmine policy could be created with the ITDR - Active Directory attack detection module to detect credential misuse, entitlement exposures and privilege escalation activities against AD via the Landmine Agent.

quotes: August 31, 2023

You can create a Windows landmine policy and configure the ITDR - Active Directory (AD) attack detection module to detect credential misuse, entitlement exposures, and privilege escalation activities against AD via the Landmine Agent.

2023-08-31-ad-scan-via-landmine.statement: In the release note dated August 31, 2023: AD domains could be scanned via a Microsoft Windows landmine agent to discover identity vulnerabilities such as AS-REP roasting and kerberoasting.

quotes: August 31, 2023
You can scan AD domains via a Microsoft Windows landmine agent to discover identity vulnerabilities, such as AS-REP roasting and kerberoasting attacks.

current-behaviour.title: Which release-note entries still describe how ITDR behaves today
current-behaviour.detail: Each claim says what the release note dated at its start said. The notes do not say whether a later release changed or removed the behaviour, and the current help pages for the same features may differ (for example the dashboard and tab names the notes record as renamed).
